q: What is the running time of KMP for a text of length n and a pattern of length m?
explain: Computing the prefix function takes O(m) and scanning the text takes O(n). The text pointer never moves backwards.

q: π[q] in KMP's prefix function is the length of…
options: the longest proper prefix of P[0..q] that is also a suffix of P[0..q]
the longest suffix of the whole pattern
the number of times P[q] occurs in P
the shift used by the naive algorithm
explain: Such a prefix-and-suffix is called a border. 'Proper' means the whole string itself does not count.

q: What is the prefix function of 'ababaca'?
explain: Borders of each prefix: a (0), ab (0), aba (1: a), abab (2: ab), ababa (3: aba), ababac (0), ababaca (1: a).

q: What is the prefix function of 'aaaa'?
explain: 'aa' has border 'a' (1), 'aaa' has 'aa' (2), and 'aaaa' has 'aaa' (3). The first entry is always 0.

q: KMP has matched q > 0 pattern characters, and the next text character mismatches P[q]. What does KMP do?
options: Sets q ← π[q − 1] and compares again, without moving in the text
Moves the text pointer back q positions
Restarts with q = 0 at the next text position
Skips m characters of the text
explain: The longest border of the matched part tells KMP how much of the pattern still lines up. It may repeat this fall-back several times.

q: How many times does KMP find 'abab' in 'abababab', counting overlapping matches?
explain: The matches start at positions 0, 2 and 4. After each match KMP continues from q = π[3] = 2, so it finds overlapping occurrences.

q: In KMP, the index into the text never decreases.
explain: True. Only the pattern index q falls back. That is why the matching phase is O(n).

q: Which input makes the naive matcher take Θ(n·m) comparisons, where KMP takes O(n + m)?
options: T and P with no letters in common
explain: The naive matcher compares almost all of P at every position before failing on the final b. KMP reuses the matched a's through π.

q: What is π[0], the prefix-function value of the first character, for any pattern?
explain: A one-character string has no non-empty proper prefix, so its longest border is empty.

q: The prefix function of a string s of length n is computed. What is the shortest period of s?
explain: If s has a border of length b, then s repeats with period n − b. The longest border gives the shortest period. For example, 'abcabcabcab' has π = 8 at the end, so its period is 11 − 8 = 3.
